questions.text: What story do you tell yourself about who you are when you finally stop taking care of everyone else?
Where does your body hold the anger that you keep hidden to protect the peace around you?
What does it cost you to carry the weight of an obligation that nobody asked your permission to give you?
What would happen if you believed that having human limits is a natural right instead of a personal failure?
Who taught you that your life counts for less simply because you do not have a spouse or children?
What would it feel like if someone looked at you and saw a person with her own life instead of just a caretaker?
What small piece of your freedom do you miss the most when every single hour belongs to someone else?
What becomes possible when you allow yourself to speak your truth out loud without managing everyone else's reactions?
